title: Billboarding broken at far distances from origin
body:
### Tested versions

- Tested in v4.6.dev.double.custom_build [837c948d9] which is basically building the master branch but with the LimboAI engine module and using a custom updating script (my "changes" can be found [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...ARez2:godot-double:arez2/changes) )

The build command (taken from my `UPDATE.sh`) is:
```
scons platform=linuxbsd precision=double arch=x86_64
```

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev.double (837c948d9) - Ubuntu 25.04 25.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT (RADV NAVI32) - AMD Ryzen 9 7900X3D 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 61.01 GiB memory

### Issue description

I am making a space game where I have very large distances. One day I wanted to add an Explosion visual effect using GPUParticles3D and noticed that billboarding produces "jittering" of the meshes when the node is very far away from the origin.

Experimenting with it, it's not just the "Particle Billboard" mode that is broken, but any Billboard mode.

I thought Godot uses some workarounds to emulate double precision even for shaders, but those don't seem to be working here. Maybe I misunderstand something though.

Here is a video taken out of my project: https://vimeo.com/1126486753

### Steps to reproduce

- Get a double precision build
- Edit a project
- Add a MeshInstance3D or GPUParticles3D (in the MRP I use a CubeMesh with size (1,1,1) but it shouldn't matter which mesh)
- set the mesh material `billboard_mode` to anything other than "Disabled"
- Move the node to `x=500000` or some other far distance from the origin
- Orbit the camera to see the jitter

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[billboarding-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22866284/billboarding-mrp.zip)
